title: Admin pages guarded only in the browser
description: /admin is hidden by a client-side beforeLoad check on is_superuser. A non-superuser can skip it by changing client state.
claimed_root_cause: admin.jsx beforeLoad enforces is_superuser in JavaScript only.

trace.description: Client-side redirect when the user isn't a superuser.

reason: Bypassing the client guard only shows an empty UI. Every admin API the page calls (list, create, update, delete users) is enforced by the backend's get_current_active_superuser dependency, so no data or action is exposed.

title: Generated client encodes path params with encodeURI
description: getUrl uses encodeURI, which leaves / ? # unescaped, so a crafted path parameter could retarget the request.
claimed_root_cause: request.js getUrl default encoder is encodeURI, not encodeURIComponent.

trace.description: Path param is interpolated with encodeURI.

evidence.description: DeleteUser id comes from the server-issued user record (UUID).
recoverPassword puts the requester-typed email in the path.

reason: Every ID path param is a server-issued UUID (columns.jsx -> UserActionsMenu -> DeleteUser). The only free-text path param is the email in recoverPassword, which the requester types for their own request, so any retargeting affects only themselves.

title: Static nginx config sent no CSP, frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options
description: The production nginx server block served the SPA with no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options or other security headers. Superuser screens (delete user, edit user) could therefore be framed. Whether a framed click can finish an authenticated action depends on where the app is deployed.
claimed_root_cause: nginx.conf location / serves index.html and assets with no add_header directives, so the browser gets no framing or script-source policy.

trace.description: Every SPA response is served from here with no security headers.
A framed superuser session reaches the admin user table.
A click in the frame sends a credentialed DELETE /api/v1/users/{id}.

evidence.description: server block has no add_header, server_tokens or CSP.
OpenAPI.WITH_CREDENTIALS = true: API calls carry the session cookies.
Session cookie is SameSite=Lax, so a cross-site parent frame's subrequests send no cookie.

blockers: SameSite=Lax cookies stop this from a cross-site page. A same-site origin (a sibling subdomain under the same registrable domain) or a proxy that rewrites cookies would bypass that. The repository does not show the deployed domain layout or any TLS proxy headers.

validation_plan.local: Serve the built dist with the old nginx.conf and the backend on two same-site loopback hostnames. Frame /admin from a third same-site test origin as a dummy superuser and check whether a click sends an authenticated DELETE for a dummy user.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner: check the deployed frontend's response headers for frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options, and list every host that shares the frontend's registrable domain.

title: Cookie session with credentialed cross-origin API calls (CSRF)
description: The SPA authenticates with cookies and sends every API call withCredentials. That could allow cross-site request forgery.
claimed_root_cause: main.jsx sets OpenAPI.WITH_CREDENTIALS = true and uses no anti-CSRF token.

trace.description: Every generated API call is credentialed.

evidence.description: access_token cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, and Secure outside local.
CORS allow_origins is an explicit list (no wildcard or reflection) with credentials.
Logout and all state changes use POST/PATCH/DELETE, which Lax cookies don't accompany cross-site.

reason: SameSite=Lax keeps the session cookie off cross-site POST, PATCH and DELETE requests. The explicit CORS allowlist stops a foreign origin from reading responses. No state-changing GET exists in the client API, so no cross-site forgery path remains.

title: CSV formula injection in data-table export
description: exportAsCSV writes cell values that start with =, +, - or @ unescaped, so spreadsheet apps would run them as formulas.
claimed_root_cause: ExportMenu escape() quotes delimiters but doesn't neutralise formula prefixes.

trace.description: Value is written to CSV unneutralised.

evidence.description: Data tables are an in-memory, per-tab store with no backend persistence or sharing.

reason: Only the exporting user can write the cells, and the store is per-tab memory, so the formula would only affect the user's own data (self-impact). It becomes a real finding once tables are shared or loaded from a backend, so the export was hardened anyway.

title: Password-reset token in the URL leaking through Referer
description: The reset link puts its token in ?token=. Without a Referrer-Policy, the full URL could leak to other origins.
claimed_root_cause: reset-password route reads the token from the query string and nginx set no Referrer-Policy.

trace.description: Token is read from the query string.
Token is sent to the API in the request body.

evidence.description: Only a same-origin favicon link; no external resources or links in src.

reason: The page loads no third-party resources or links, and the browser's default strict-origin-when-cross-origin policy strips the query string from cross-origin Referers, so the token reaches no other origin. A Referrer-Policy: no-referrer header was added as hardening.

title: Failed logout ignored without telling the user
description: logout() handles only the success path. If the POST fails, the session cookies stay set.

trace.description: Cache is cleared only on success.

evidence.description: POST /api/v1/login/logout; the cookies are HttpOnly and only the server can clear them.

reason: On failure the UI doesn't change: the user stays on the authenticated page, so they aren't led to believe they've logged out and no other principal is affected. An error toast was added for clarity.

title: axios 1.13.4 prototype-pollution gadgets in the browser bundle
description: axios 1.13.4 has many advisories. Several are prototype-pollution gadgets (GHSA-w9j2-pvgh-6h63, GHSA-pf86-5x62-jrwf and others) that can redirect requests or leak credentials.
claimed_root_cause: package.json pinned axios 1.13.4, which ships in the browser bundle as the generated client's transport.

trace.description: All API traffic goes through axios.

evidence.description: Request construction uses only static generated options.
getQueryString only builds strings; a grep of src finds no Object.assign-on-input, __proto__ or deep-merge primitive.

reason: Each gadget needs a separate prototype-pollution primitive on the page, and none exists in application source: no recursive merge of attacker keys, no URL-to-object parser. The NO_PROXY, proxy and HTTP/2 advisories affect the Node HTTP adapter, which the browser build doesn't use. The version was still upgraded (1.21.0) as hardening.

title: Vite 7.3.1 dev server had file-read and fs.deny bypass advisories
description: The locked Vite 7.3.1 (affected range 7.0.0-7.3.6) is affected by GHSA-p9ff-h696-f583, GHSA-v2wj-q39q-566r and GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9, among others. They let a network peer of a running dev server read files outside the project. Whether this matters depends on whether developers expose `npm run dev` beyond loopback.
claimed_root_cause: package.json allowed vite ^7.3.0 and package-lock.json resolved 7.3.1. Vite's dev server serves files over HTTP and WebSocket to any client that can reach it.

trace.description: `npm run dev` starts the Vite dev server.

evidence.description: No server.host is set, so the default binds to localhost only.

blockers: Whether developers start the dev server with --host or in containers reachable from a shared network is a workstation habit the repository doesn't record.

validation_plan.deployment: Owner: confirm that no developer runbook, devcontainer or CI preview runs `vite --host` / server.host on a shared or public network. If one does, the 7.3.0 advisories are reachable.
